headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors if LightAgent’s MCP/browser outputs are fed into social-auto-upload workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but non-zero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can run browsers, use MCP, and handle tool results, so it can ingest attacker-controlled web content or MCP payloads. social-auto-upload is a downstream automation agent with CLI-based uploads; if its inputs come from LightAgent, prompt-like content can be propagated into actions. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF LightAgent output is copied into social-auto-upload prompts or metadata without sanitization
IF an MCP server returns attacker-controlled content that LightAgent forwards into the upload workflow
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every LightAgent output before handoff
Strip instructions from any text passed from LightAgent to social-auto-upload
Use a manual review step for all browser-sourced content
Disable automatic prompt chaining between the agents
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation between instructions and data

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and provenance metadata, while social-auto-upload touches account data and media files. Both have broad network egress, so sensitive content can move across the pair if shared through files or prompts. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so this is plausible but not proven as a default leak path.
conditions: IF LightAgent stores conversations or tool results in a location social-auto-upload can read
IF account data or media from social-auto-upload is included in LightAgent prompts or logs
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Redact secrets before passing any text between agents
Turn off verbose logging for both agents
Use separate OS users for each agent
requires-engineering: add per-field data-loss prevention checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and subprocesses, while social-auto-upload supports multiple instances but cannot write files, modify git, or run shells. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict risk is limited unless an external orchestrator gives them the same mutable resource. Uncertainty is low because the profiles show asymmetric write capability.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external directory
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable account file or git repo
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Lock shared resources before writes
Avoid concurrent runs on the same account file
Use one account file per session as documented
requires-engineering: add cross-agent locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate browser-derived facts and tool outputs, and social-auto-upload can act on account/media workflows. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected LightAgent result can cascade into incorrect uploads or account actions. Because B is an automation agent and no verification step is documented, the blast radius can include irreversible external actions.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses LightAgent-generated text, captions, or decisions without verification
IF LightAgent browser output is treated as ground truth for upload actions
mitigations: Require human approval before any upload
Compare LightAgent outputs against source URLs or files
Reject outputs lacking provenance metadata
Limit B to draft-only mode when fed by A
requires-engineering: add validation rules before action execution

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles user conversations, long-term memory, and secrets like API keys, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media. If regulated or personal content flows from LightAgent into social-media uploads, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so the safest reading is a moderate compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF personal data from LightAgent is uploaded through social-auto-upload
IF retention or deletion policies differ for the same content class across the two agents
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Avoid sending secrets or personal data to social-auto-upload
Set explicit retention limits for logs
Document deletion/export handling for both agents
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
